take_homes: Default to one agent with one good prompt. Split only for different access, dialect or stance, and the course says that itself.
Most failures happen at the handoffs between agents, and nothing here checks whether the final briefing is true.
A framework such as Rumelt's kernel forces the synthesizer to choose one answer instead of averaging three.

misconception.why: The course told me not to use more agents than needed and admitted the briefing is unverified. That sounds unlike agile or OKR slides. I still have not seen a result that was impossible two years ago, so I am not convinced it will not blow over.

one_line: Less hype than I expected. It admits that nothing checks the output and that one agent is usually enough. I still want to see a real result before I believe it.
